title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

🎉 Public Hours at the Commons 🎉

Every Sunday, the Commons opens to the public — no membership required. Come co-work, connect, create, or just explore the space at your own pace. ✨

📍 Where: 540 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna, basement level)

RSVP and we'll email you your entry code ahead of time — so you can let yourself straight in when you arrive.

Public Hours are self-guided — come in, settle in, and make the space your own. Weekends are usually unstaffed, so there's no check-in desk or guided tour. Our members are glad to answer questions about the space; for anything else — including guided tours, which we don't offer as drop-ins — email hello@thesfcommons.com ahead of time.

Your entry code comes by email. Once you RSVP, we'll send you a personal QR code — that's your key for the day. Keep it handy on your phone (and check spam if you don't see it).

title: The Essence Experience: The Power of Perspective
description:
You know what it's like to be you, but you don't know what it's like to be with you.

Every person you've ever met knows something about you that you don't. Not because they know you better, but because they know what it's like to be with you.

Gather for a guided journey of observation, reflection, and conversation that invites you to explore a new way of understanding yourself and others.

Most of us spend our lives asking questions like...

• Why have I been successful?
• What makes me different?
• What don't I know about myself that's important to know?

We often look inward for the answers, focusing on our intentions, efforts, hopes, and stories. But another perspective shapes every relationship, conversation, and opportunity we have: the experience others have of us.

The Essence Experience begins with a different question: What if the answers to understanding ourselves start with how we're experienced by others?

Through a series of thoughtfully designed experiences, you'll practice receiving observations with curiosity, recognize patterns across different perspectives, and gain insight into the qualities that have shaped your life all along.

The qualities that shape your life most profoundly are often the ones you take for granted.

This experience isn't about becoming someone new. It's about discovering more of who you've been all along. You'll leave with fresh insight into your strengths, gifts, and leadership qualities, while learning to see the possibilities and potential in the people around you.

Come curious. Leave seeing yourself and others differently.

Michael Tertes is a leadership coach, speaker, and facilitator who has spent nearly 20 years helping people discover and express what is extraordinary about who they already are. Through his Leadership Essence™ work, he helps leaders uncover their unique qualities so they can lead more authentically, embrace their distinctive impact, and bring more of themselves to their leadership.

His signature workshop, The Essence Experience™, reveals a profound human blind spot. We rarely recognize the unique impact we have on others or communicate the impact they have on us. His work invites people to move beyond a culture of correction toward one that also practices recognition, creating deeper connection, greater self-awareness, and more authentic relationships.

Michael is based in Berkeley, California.

www.MichaelTertes.com

🌁 Look out at the San Francisco skyline and you’ll see some of the most recognizable landmarks in the world. But have you ever stopped to wonder why they exist?
What is Sutro Tower actually for? What’s the real story behind Coit Tower? And how did a grand Roman-style rotunda end up next to a lagoon in the Marina?
In this lecture, Hannah Blazei, KPIX journalist and founder of Good Stories San Francisco, takes us behind the city’s most iconic silhouettes to uncover the surprising, sometimes strange stories of how they came to be. Hannah spends her time digging up the hidden history all around us, and she has a gift for turning forgotten details into stories you’ll want to retell at your next dinner party.
From world’s fairs and big personalities to bold feats of engineering, you’ll learn how the skyline we take for granted was shaped by ambition, controversy, and a few happy accidents.
Whether you’re a lifelong local or new to the Bay, you’ll never look at the skyline the same way again. 🏙️

title: 🧠 The Thought Experiment Lab
description:
Note: while there are many guests listed in the RSVP, most of these are carried over from previous events in this series. We don't expect much more than 30 to attend.

"Imagination without reason is mere fancy, but reason without imagination is sterile. That is partly why scientists and philosophers alike have always used imaginary scenarios to help sharpen their ideas and push them to their limits." - The Pig that Wants to be Eaten, by Julian Baggini

For this meeting (December 2), we'll be discussing the whether we can know things by intuition and how we might know things like:

• 2 + 2 = 4
• A belief chosen at random cannot be justified
• An action is free only if you could have done otherwise
• It is wrong to cause suffering for no reason

Please review this very brief primer on the norms of philosophical discussion: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Gj3HesfWz4A2kEAMSY0x7hNxvJZNtiCexUeilJXVak8/edit?usp=sharing

• It is highly recommended to read this article: https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/intuition/

• Read sections 1.3, 2.1-2.3, and 3.1-3.5

Some examples of topics we've discussed at past meetings:

• Do you survive being teleported?
• Is God required to have morality?
• What are the limits of free speech?
• Is it moral to breed pigs that want to be eaten?
• Should crimes be punished before they happen?
• Are some pleasures more noble than others?
• Do immoral people just have bad luck?
• Is monogamy unethical?
• Is the existence of evil a problem for belief in God?
• Should we try to become immortal?
• Are we obligated to do much more to the world's poor?
• Is it okay to deliberately create a disabled child?
• Is it permissible to kill and eat animals?
• Should we enter the experience machine?
• Is science the only source of knowledge?
• Is what is right or wrong a matter of opinion?
• On what basis should we care about the environment?
• Can we know we are not brains in a vat?
• What is a potential person worth?
• What is gender?
• What is philosophy and how is it done?
• Is abortion morally permissible?
• Does philosophy make assumptions?
• Is evolutionary psychology a legitimate science?
• Should paid organ donation be permitted?
• Can we have knowledge without certainty?
• Is adult consensual incest always immoral?
• Is everything we do ultimately motivated by self-interest?
• Is it immoral to have children?
• Are there good arguments against objective morality?
• Should we use genetic therapies to increase intelligence?
• Is it morally permissible to select your child's race?
• Does free will require the ability to do otherwise?
• Do our lives have meaning?
• Can dating preferences be irrational or discriminatory?
• Is happiness the only thing that matters to one's well-being?
• Was the universe created by God?
• Is morality only about the greatest good for the greatest number?
• How important is it to preserve minority cultures?

We'll be meeting in the 540 Room. Contact me by text if you're having trouble finding the location.

On the Wednesdays when we're not running this event, we'll often be having similar discussions here: https://lu.ma/shortstories

title: Where Do "I" End? Complexity Science as Contemplative Practice
description:
🌿 About Event

A flock of starlings turns as one shape that no single bird is steering. Your sense of "me" might work a bit the same way - and so might a forest, or the distributed AI systems many of us now spend our days talking to. After a PhD in physics and years in complex systems research, I keep finding the science pointing at things contemplatives have said for a long time: that where "I" end and the world begins is more a choice of how we look than a fact. I don't fully know what to make of that yet - which is partly why I run these circles.

We'll start with a short, plain intro to a few ideas from complexity science - emergence, self-organization, how many simple things can together do something smart. Then we slow down into a meditative discussion circle, honoring the pre-conceptual silence as much as the ideas. Something between a philosophy salon and a sharing circle.

Why now: we're building minds out of many simple parts, and handing them more and more of our attention. It seems like a good moment to look closely at what a "self" is made of - ours included.

🕰 Flow / Schedule

2:00 - 2:10 Arrival + tea

2:10 - 2:30 Landing meditation, a round of names, and introduction to complex systems thinking

2:30 - 3:50 Meditative discussion - a few sentences each, silence in between, being together with the ideas in open awareness. I will introduce a few more key concepts throughout to feed the conversation.

3:50 - 4:00 Harvesting and Closing

4:00 - 5:00 Mingling

👥 Facilitators

Name: Pavel Chvykov

Bio: Pavel is a physicist who got curious why meditation and complexity science keep describing the same world in different words. He runs a research community where scientists and contemplatives work on that question together, and he facilitates circles where it gets explored out loud, and in silence.

Website: complexitycontemplation.org
pchvykov.com ·

💫 Who This Is For

Anyone who has felt the edges of the self go soft in meditation and wondered what science makes of it - and anyone in science, tech or AI quietly asking what minds are. Meditators curious about science, scientists and builders who sit, and the plainly curious. No science or meditation background needed.

🎒 What to Bring (Optional)

Just yourself, and a question you're living with lately.

💛 Suggested Donation / Exchange

Suggested donation: $5-10 at the door to support space stewardship.

The Commons is a community-based "Fourth Place" that catalyzes each member's path to authenticity, full self-expression, and aliveness - rooted in the belief that community is essential to that journey. Navigating work right now can feel… confusing.

What do I actually want?

If you've ever felt lost, restless or unsure whether your current path still fits - you're not alone.

Join us for Purpose Alignment Circle, a space for candid conversations about vocation, purpose, and what it means to build a career that actually feels aligned with who you are.

This isn't another networking event or career playbook with all the answers.

We're excited to welcome our guest facilitator Diane, founder of Deep Currents Consulting and former Associate Director of Stanford Living Education, where she led the Leadership, Community Building, and Social Change (LEAD) program.

With a passion for helping people live and lead with purpose, Diane has taught more than 25 courses and worked with over 1,000 Stanford students, including through her signature course, Living on Purpose.

Before that, she spent two decades as a senior qualitative researcher at Stanford Graduate School of Education, studying holistic education.

This is for you if: 💭

• You're questioning whether your 9–5 is still working for you
• You're considering a career pivot
• You want to start your own company
• You have a passion project you're exploring alongside your corporate job
• You're thinking about taking a sabbatical
• OR you just returned from a sabbatical and are figuring out what's next
• You want to reconnect with a sense of purpose in your work
• You don't have the answer yet - but you're curious enough to explore

• You're looking for a step-by-step formula for finding your “dream job”
• You want someone else to tell you what career you should pursue

A weekly space for real conversations, meaningful connection, and a deeper sense of belonging.

🌿 About This Gathering

Maybe you've got plenty of people in your life, but still sometimes feel lonely. Maybe you find it hard to move beyond small talk and social scripts. Maybe you sometimes struggle to feel like you truly belong, even when you're surrounded by people. Or maybe you're simply curious about what makes some relationships and communities feel easy, genuine, and nourishing — while others don't.

Each week, we'll explore a different aspect of connection and belonging: loneliness, vulnerability, authenticity, being seen, boundaries, desire, conflict, and what gets in the way of feeling connected and at home with others.

title: Somatic Breathwork Journey: Emotional Release, Clarity & Nervous System Reset
description:
Come breathe, release, & reset...

Somatic Breathwork is an embodiment experience designed to take you out of your thinking mind and into the deep intelligence of your body — where true healing, clarity, and release happen. It allows your body to express and discharge stored emotions, stress, and old narratives that may be weighing you down.

Somatic Breathwork uses circular connected breathing together with rhythmic music to produce a cathartic emotional release. This release may be in the form of moving, shaking, yelling, crying, laughing, or simply deep stillness.

It gives your body the opportunity to express emotions or actions that may otherwise be unacceptable in modern social settings, allowing your nervous system to process traumas and restore balance.

Using the breath, you’ll engage your body’s innate ability to heal — sweeping out any defenses, blockages, restrictions, or pains that hold you back from showing up as your truest self.

Many participants experience profound emotional release, newfound clarity, and a grounded sense of calm even after a single session.

This experience is designed to:

• Move you out of your mind and into your body's electrical network
• Release stuck energy, emotions, or trauma responses
• Reset your nervous system into grounded calm and clarity
• Break old patterns and reconnect you to your authentic self
• Increase compassion, presence, and emotional resilience
• Support cathartic release in a safe, guided container

Participants often report:

• Deep emotional release
• More calm, peace, and clarity
• Release of anger, grief, frustration, or stagnant energy
• Increased presence, awareness, and intuition
• Breakthrough insights about their life, patterns, and purpose
• Feeling more open, soft, and connected to themselves and others

What to expect:

Whether you're seeking release, clarity, a reset, or simply a moment to reconnect with yourself — this session is for you.

Please bring a journal and water bottle, and wear comfortable clothes.

NOTE: Please be on time for this session — doors will close promptly and there will be NO LATE ENTRIES!

About Anna Bolender:

Anna Bolender is a certified Somatic Embodiment & Intuitive Life Coach, Somatic Breathwork and Quantum Wellness Practitioner, Reiki Master, and lifelong student of holistic health and well-being.

Through her coaching programs and workshops, Anna guides others to return home to themselves — releasing what keeps them stuck, reconnecting with their body and inner wisdom, and creating real, lasting transformation from the inside out.

Blending somatics, energy healing, quantum wellness, and mindset work, she helps clients break free from self-sabotaging patterns, repattern their nervous system, and cultivate simple daily rituals that support a fulfilling, grounded, and aligned life.

Anna’s mission is to empower others to feel connected, alive, and radiant — no matter what life brings.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

title: dorkbot @ TIAT !!! with talks from Ken Goldberg, Scott Snibbe, and Ahna Girshick
description:
people doing strange things with electricity.

Our speakers this time are Ken Goldberg, Scott Snibbe, and Ahna Girshick!

More about our speakers:

ϟ Ahna Girshick - The Grammar of Seeing: From Nature to Machines

What if the way we see the world is shaped by a hidden visual grammarâ€”one shared with animals and machine vision models? Our visual systems evolved to extract meaningful patterns from nature, detecting edges, shapes, textures, and objects. Machine vision models, trained on images of our world, develop their own visual vocabulary, revealing surprising parallels with biological vision. In this talk, artist and vision scientist Ahna Girshick explores the building blocks of biological and machine perception, and how she transforms the glyphs of seeing into art.

Ahna Girshick is a visual artist and vision scientist who investigates the visual grammar used by humans, machines, and nature. Her art combines her research with data, algorithms, glass, mirrors, photos and video. In 2025 she was commissioned by Google (SF) to create a three-story site-specific glass installation. She holds a PhD from UC Berkeley in Vision Science, and was a postdoctoral fellow at NYU. She designed and taught an illusions class for UC Berkeleyâ€™s Cognitive Science program, and has recently given public talks at The Commonwealth Club of California and The Internet Archive

https://lightdark.org

ϟ Ken Goldberg - Agentic Robotics

There have been two approaches to controlling robots: (1) model-based, where engineers model, program and tune each application, and (2) model-free, where large VLA or ACT models are trained on large datasets of physical demonstrations. Agentic Robotics (AR) is a third approach. In Agentic Robotics, multi-agent LLM systems write, test, diagnose and iteratively improve structured robot programs, largely offline, and increasingly build the simulations those programs are tested in. This website places it between the model-based and model-free traditions, describes the pipeline we are building at AUTOLab, and lists current projects.

Ken Goldberg is William S. Floyd Distinguished Professor of Engineering at UC Berkeley, President of the international Robot Learning Foundation, member of the US National Academy of Engineering, IEEE Fellow, co-founder and Editor-in-Chief emeritus of the IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering (T-ASE), Co-Founder of Jacobi Robotics, and Co-Founder/Chief Scientist of Ambi Robotics. Ken leads research in robotics and automation: grasping, manipulation, and learning for applications in warehouses, homes, agriculture, and robot-assisted surgery. He is Distinguished Professor of IEOR, EECS, and Art Practice. Ken has published 10 US patents, over 450 refereed papers, and has presented over 600 invited lectures to academic and corporate audiences.

http://goldberg.berkeley.edu

ϟ Scott Snibbe - Hidden Geometries

Scott Snibbe will talk about his recent generative art series Hidden Geometries. The series draws on the sacred geometric grids underlying Tibetan Buddhist thangka paintings to explore whether contemporary dynamic abstract art can induce meditative experiences similar to the inspiration of its thousand-year-old tradition. Coming off a recent residency at Headlands Center for the Arts, he will show new works for projection, LED displays, and paintings using traditional mineral pigment techniques. Heâ€™ll share the process behind these works and explore how technological art can break our delusions of separateness and cultivate deeper connection with ourselves and others.

Scott Snibbe is a new media artist, author, and meditation teacher. His pioneering interactive art is held in the collections of New Yorkâ€™s Museum of Modern Art and the Whitney Museum of American Art and has been exhibited worldwide. He has collaborated with BjÃ¶rk, Philip Glass, Beck, and James Cameron on innovative intersections of art, music, and technology. A longtime practitioner and teacher of Tibetan Buddhism, Snibbe is the author of How to Train a Happy Mind (2024), featuring a foreword by the Dalai Lama.

description:
Some experiences change the shape of us.

They leave behind questions, fragments, memories, feelings, and stories we may not always know what to do with.

Sometimes, making meaning begins by giving those things somewhere to go.

This gathering is an invitation to explore creative expression as a way of processing what we carry. Through writing, art, movement, reflection, and conversation, we'll make space for what can been difficult to name and explore creating meaning together.

This is a space to witness, create, and connect, and to remember that even our hardest experiences can sit alongside meaning, movement, and possibility.

What to expect: We'll open with a short grounding, Nick Silva will share his story, and then make time for writing or art with prompts. Sharing is always optional. You're welcome to create quietly and just listen. No artistic experience needed. Materials will be provided.

This is a peer and creative space, not therapy or crisis care.

Content note: We'll be talking about suicide and self-harm, along with hope and resilience. You can step out at any time. There will be a quiet space, and Chelsea will be there just to offer support. If you need to talk to someone right now, you can call or text 988, any time.

title: Big Brain: The El Niño, Explained
description:
🌊 A historic El Niño is here. What does that actually mean for us?
CBS News Bay Area meteorologist Zoe Mintz breaks down the science behind El Niño, from how it forms to how it influences weather patterns across the United States. She’ll revisit previous El Niño years and their impacts before exploring what makes this year’s unusually warm Pacific Ocean so remarkable.
Zoe will then bring the science closer to home, unpacking California’s exceptionally warm coastal waters, record-high sea levels, the science behind Kelvin waves, and why our king tides are reaching such extreme heights.
What happens when a winter storm coincides with a king tide? Which Bay Area neighborhoods are most vulnerable to flooding? And how can we prepare?
You’ll leave with a deeper understanding of one of Earth’s most influential climate phenomena and what it could mean for our own backyard this winter. 🌎

Write & Mingle: 6pm to 7pm
Share on Stage: 7pm to 8pm
Drink & Discuss: 8pm to 9pm

title: Huney Knuckles
description:
HUGE NOISE, world class musicianship, mind-bending solos, and uber funky jams
Kevin Wong, Darian Gray, Tony Peebles & Bian Sheu
9pm-12:30am / $7
The newest kids on the block, the Huney Knuckles (formerly the Black Star Pirates) combines the left hand keyboard bass wizardry of Kevin Wong with the indomitable pocket of Darian Gray, touring drummer for Booker T Jones for the past 14 years. Founded in early 2021, the Huney Knuckles were birthed during the quarantine at Black Star Pirate BBQ when they teamed up with Grammy winning saxophonist Tony Peebles & Virtuoso guitarist Brian Sheu to bring the joy of live music to one of the first places in town to host socially distanced outdoor live music. Fusing watertight grooves with high energy shreds that will make you want to jump out of your seat, this 4-piece has made a huge noise in the local scene, drawing new fans left & right at every show with their world class musicianship, mind-bending solos, and uber-funky jams.
